ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are two spinners. The spinner on the left is divided into 4 equal sectors, and the numbers are respectively 5, 3, 8, 4; the spinner on the right is divided into 3 equal sectors, and the numbers are respectively 6, 9, 7. Each time the two spinners are spun, each has a pointer select one number. Then reason: Among the left spinner, the even numbers are 8, 4, a total of 2; the odd numbers are 5, 3, a total of 2, so the probability that the left spinner selects an even number is 1/2, and the probability that it selects an odd number is 1/2. Among the right spinner, the even number is 6, a total of 1; the odd numbers are 9, 7, a total of 2, so the probability that the right spinner selects an even number is 1/3, and the probability that it selects an odd number is 2/3. The sum of the two numbers is even if and only if the two numbers are both even or both odd. Therefore the probability is (1/2)(1/3) + (1/2)(2/3) = 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2.

method.method_draft: First inspect the image: the left spinner is divided into four equal sectors labeled 5, 3, 8, and 4; the right spinner is divided into three equal sectors labeled 6, 9, and 7. From the text, each spin selects one number from each wheel, and the goal is the probability that their sum is even. Classify by parity: left wheel has 2 even numbers and 2 odd numbers, so P(left even)=1/2 and P(left odd)=1/2. Right wheel has 1 even number and 2 odd numbers, so P(right even)=1/3 and P(right odd)=2/3. An even sum occurs when both selected numbers have the same parity, so compute P(even sum)=P(E,E)+P(O,O)=(1/2)(1/3)+(1/2)(2/3)=1/6+1/3=1/2.
